messages:
Priya Shah: Hey team — have a DSAR where user requests deletion of all their personal data. They say historical backups/snapshots contain their data and those backups are KMS-encrypted. Need play for retention exception + RBAC/audit evidence. cc @Legal

Omar Li: Is this for hosted API customer or a private deployment?

Priya Shah: Hosted API, tenant id T-4321. No legal hold flags on the account as far as I can see. User wants confirmation within 72h.

Elaine Wu: Quick checklist: 1) Confirm legal hold/subpoena 2) Inventory backups/snapshots & KMS key usage 3) Plan deletion steps & evidence export 4) RBAC approval chain and audit trail. Don’t rotate/delete CMKs without legal ok.

Jordan (DevOps): For snapshot/object deletion we can run discovery and then delete. Example AWS commands (ops-only):
```
aws ec2 delete-snapshot --snapshot-id snap-0abc123
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-backups/tenant/T-4321/ --recursive
```
Also ensure CloudTrail events are exported for the time window and our internal audit-log contains the operator id and runbook link.

Priya Shah: If we follow that, how long until we can produce a deletion proof to the user? They asked for 72h.

Omar Li: Discovery script: 2-4h. Deletion + audit export: 1-3h. Packaging evidence and legal sign-off adds variable time — if Legal approves quickly we should be within 24-48h.

Legal Team: @Priya please attach the DSAR ticket + proof of identity. We need to confirm no pending litigation/subpoena. If clear, we will approve the deletion.

Elaine Wu: For RBAC requirements we should follow the dsar-delete runbook: requires two approvers (security + ops) and creates an immutable audit record. Internal API call used by runbook: `POST /internal/dsar/requests/{id}/approve` — this call is logged and triggers security-bot.

security-bot: [AUTO] dsar-delete request 8421 approved by Elaine Wu and Omar Li at 2026-03-20T13:42:19Z; action scheduled.

Jordan (DevOps): Post-deletion plan: 1) run final verification listing (object ids + checksums) 2) export CloudTrail event ids and S3 deletion confirmation 3) store evidence bundle in evidence-bucket/encrypted/tenant-T-4321/ with 90d retention, signed by HSM. We'll redact PII from the bundle before sending to user.

Priya Shah: Important note on KMS: rotating a CMK vs deleting it. Rotating keys is reversible; deleting keys is destructive. For hosted multi-tenant CMKs we can't delete the key if shared. If the customer used a customer-managed key (CMK) we need additional steps and explicit consent.

Omar Li: Confirmed — our default is platform-managed keys; we only have customer-managed CMKs for a few enterprise tenants. If this is platform-managed, deletion of objects + snapshots is the right approach; do not delete/disable platform CMKs.

Priya Shah: What fields do regulators expect in the audit export to accept proof? I propose: user id, tenant id, operator id(s), operation type, resource ids, timestamps, checksums of deleted objects, and link to approval ticket. Anything else?

Elaine Wu: That list is good. Add the approval chain (approver names & timestamps), the runbook version, and a signed hash of the evidence bundle (HSM signature). Keep the exported payload free of PII — use stable identifiers.

Priya Shah: Great. I'll attach the DSAR and verification materials once Legal confirms. Will kick off discovery script right after approval. Thanks all :+1:
